mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has risen in each of the last three weeks, from -37.0 to -33.4 percent below baseline, and station footfall recovery leads discretionary retail footfall by one to two weeks; continued transit normalization therefore lifts RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean of -30.1 over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.6 points over three consecutive weeks (t-3w -37.0 to t-0w -33.4)
failure_condition: TRANSIT continues to rise week-on-week while the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below its prior-28-day mean of -30.1.

mechanism_narrative: Once the WORKPLACES weekly mean crosses above -22.0 percent below baseline, office density is high enough to regenerate weekday lunchtime and after-work retail trips, so RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean rises above -22.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES crossed -22.0 in t-0w at -21.6 after monotone gains of +1.3, +1.2, +0.5
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES exceeds -22.0, the mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days does not exceed its mean over the 14 days before the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: The joint t-0w pattern of RESIDENTIAL falling 1.3 points while TRANSIT rises 1.7 points signals households substituting out-of-home activity for staying at home; when these two series move in opposite directions by at least one point in the same week, RETAIL_REC rises over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly change <= -1.0 and TRANSIT weekly change >= +1.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w RESIDENTIAL changed -1.3 points while TRANSIT changed +1.7 points, the first joint out-of-home substitution week in the snapshot
regime_hint: late restriction phase after the mobility trough
failure_condition: Weeks with RESIDENTIAL <= -1.0 and TRANSIT >= +1.0 are followed by a 14-day mean RETAIL_REC below the level of the week preceding the signal.

mechanism_narrative: In the easing-restrictions regime with residual containment measures, a sharp one-week PARKS rebound reflects released pent-up outdoor demand that spills into adjacent retail-and-recreation venues within days, lifting RETAIL_REC on a one-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded from -34.9 at t-1w to -23.1 at t-0w, a +11.8 point jump, while RETAIL_REC rose +2.9 points
regime_hint: easing restrictions with residual containment measures
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS jumps more than 8 points, the following 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above the 7-day mean preceding the jump.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal cooling and shorter daylight from late September into October shift discretionary recreation from PARKS into indoor commercial venues; a PARKS decline from its t-0w level while TRANSIT holds steady should raise RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls back below -25.0 after the t-0w rebound
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS oscillated between -21.3 and -34.9 over four weeks, showing weather-sensitive outdoor demand
regime_hint: autumn seasonal transition under stable restrictions
failure_condition: PARKS drops below -25.0 while TRANSIT stays within 2 points of its t-0w level, yet the 28-day mean RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM holding above baseline while RETAIL_REC sits near -28 marks consumption substitution toward essentials; as grocery spending normalizes toward zero, the released discretionary budget flows back into RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the grocery series crossing down.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean falls below +1.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed non-negative in three of four weeks (3.3, 2.1, -0.3, 2.1) while RETAIL_REC held below -28 in all four weeks
failure_condition: After GROCERY_PHARM falls below +1.0, the 14-day mean RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its pre-crossing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains more than 33 points below baseline; if its week-on-week improvement stalls below half a point, weekday commuting volume stays too thin to support weekday retail trips, so RETAIL_REC mean-reverts below its t-0w level over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change falls below +0.5 points while TRANSIT stays below -30.0
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -33.4 is still 33.4 points below baseline despite three weeks of gains
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT gains less than 0.5 points while below -30.0, the next 14-day mean RETAIL_REC is above the preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The t-0w rebound in RETAIL_REC of 2.9 points coincides with an outsized PARKS swing of 11.8 points, indicating a transient single-week event rather than a level shift; absent follow-through, RETAIL_REC reverts below its t-0w level within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w RETAIL_REC changed +2.9 and PARKS changed +11.8 versus t-1w, the largest single-week swings in the snapshot
failure_condition: The 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC following a week in which PARKS rises more than 10 points equals or exceeds the level recorded in that same week.
